facts.fact: Radio Ndarason reports that at Mongo provincial hospital births are entered digitally with a Numero National d'Identification (NNI) and sent to ANATS in N'Djamena, which validates the birth act.

systems.system: Guichet unique d'enregistrement des naissances, Mongo

facts.fact: Radio Ndarason reports a digital birth registration desk at Mongo provincial hospital, backed by the government and UNICEF, serving 18 health centres within 75 km and logging 10 to 15 births a day.

TCD.note: No count or share of people holding an ID is given.

facts.fact: Radio Ndarason reports that at the Mongo hospital desk, in Guera province, birth acts are digitised with a Numero National d'Identification (NNI) and validated by ANATS, with 10 to 15 births registered a day.

TCD.note: No operator, maintainer or owner of the ID system is described.
No register keyed on the ID number is stated.
No statement on the ID system's issuance, biometrics or certification.
No local government office connection is stated.

facts.fact: Radio Ndarason reports births are entered in a secure system at the Mongo hospital registration desk and transmitted to ANATS; no deaths are mentioned.
Radio Ndarason reports the desk enters birth data at registration and ANATS receives it almost instantly by SMS for validation, after which the desk prints the act.
